h1: Seeding Rate and Plants per Hectare Calculator
summary:
Seed rate depends on the target plant population, thousand-seed weight and germination: you must sow more seed than the plants you want, because some will not establish. It returns seed rate, seeds per square metre, seeds per metre of row and plant spacing in the row, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator gives the seed weight per hectare and per square metre. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Seeding Rate and Plants per Hectare
sections.html:
Seed rate (kg/ha) = target plants × TSW ÷ 10⁶ ÷ germination ÷ establishment

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
targetplants wanted at harvestplants/ha
TSWthousand seed weightg
germinationlaboratory germination%
establishmentfield survival of germinated seed%

sections.title: How do I use the Seeding Rate and Plants per Hectare?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: target plants of 300,000 plants/ha, thousand seed weight of 40 g, germination of 92%, field establishment of 90%.

Substituting them into the formula gives seed rate of 14.49 kg/ha, seeds per square metre of 36.23 seeds/m², seeds per metre of row of 9.06 seeds/m, plant spacing in the row of 4.03e-08 cm.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Thousand seed weight is the single most useful seed-lot measurement: it converts a plant target into kilograms without any guessing.

  • Germination and field establishment are separate: a lot can germinate at 95% in the laboratory and still establish at 80% in a rough seedbed.

  • Every doubling of target population roughly halves the plants per metre of row, which is where competition, lodging and disease pressure are decided.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Using laboratory germination as if it were field establishment.
  • Confusing thousand seed weight with seed weight per plant.
  • Calculating for the target population rather than the sown population.

faq.q: How do I convert a seed rate to seeds per square metre?
faq.a: Divide the seed weight per hectare by the thousand seed weight and multiply by 1 000 ÷ 10 000.

faq.q: Why sow more than the target?
faq.a: Because a proportion of seeds never germinate or never establish.

faq.q: What does the Seeding Rate and Plants per Hectare actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns seed rate, seeds per square metre, seeds per metre of row and plant spacing in the row. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
